    "active_factor_definitions": {
      "alpha_1": "Calculates the rolling 40-day momentum rank of log-volume, then tracks the median (0.5 quantile) of this rank over a 30-day window. This effectively smooths out noisy daily volume spikes, rewarding stocks that have maintained consistently high volume momentum over a medium-term horizon.",
      "alpha_5": "Scales logarithmic dollar volume by the difference between itself and the `ohl` gap metric. This highlights periods where the absolute capital flowing into a stock fundamentally dwarfs its intraday structural price variance, indicating strong institutional sponsorship holding down volatility relative to trading magnitude.",
      "alpha_0": "The formula constructs a denominator calculating the difference between a dampened, ranked-adjusted log-volume and the raw log-volume itself. Since the denominator tends to be negative for high volume names, the division yields a negative value, which is then inverted by `Mul(-1.0, ...)` to produce a positive score for actively traded stocks. It isolates local dislocations in trading interest.",
      "alpha_2": "Measures the difference between log-volume and log-close price, approximating the number of shares traded relative to the price level. Taking the 67th percentile (upper tercile) over a fast 10-day window creates a smoothed indicator of sustained demand pressure pushing volume up faster than the stock price appreciates.",
      "alpha_3": "Computes the 20-day correlation between open-adjusted volume intensity and the daily low price. The `Mul(-1.0, ...)` operator negates this correlation. A high final score emerges when volume intensity is negatively correlated with lows, indicating heavy accumulation occurring precisely when the price drops, an algorithmic signature of strong mean-reversion support.",
      "alpha_4": "Divides the rolling 40-day rank of the spectral volume signature (vol_fft) by the Amihud illiquidity mean. Because Amihud gets larger when liquidity is worse, strong cyclical activity coupled with excellent liquidity creates a huge positive value, which the outermost `Mul(-1.0, ...)` flips into a highly negative score. The score serves as an inverted quality measure where lower (more negative) values indicate optimal liquid cyclic activity.",
      "alpha_6": "Ranks the ratio of the square root of the high price to the VWAP across the cross-section. The square root transformation dampens extreme high prints. High ranks are achieved by stocks pushing consistently higher trading ranges and execution volumes well above their average weighted execution price, signaling robust intraday buying control."
